A branch or tag named in hex digits (for example a tag `beef`) was accepted as the base commit. The base then moved with the ref and differed from clone to clone. ## The lines of the check

`src/gov/check/citations.py` is 158 lines (118 added, 20 removed against `ac952490`). `tests/unit/check/test_citations.py` is new, 199 lines, 42 cases.

## Where the check can still say "clean" without having measured

- **Nothing counted in the output.** `{"findings": []}` is the same whether many citations were compared or the commits after the base cite nothing at all. Only "no commit after the base" is an error; "commits, but zero citations" is clean.
- **The base is read from the working tree's path map (DEC-479).** Whoever moves `decision_citations_base` forward takes every earlier commit out of judgment, and the check does not report that the base moved.
- **Citation grammar.** A commit is only judged if its message matches `(ADR|DEC)-[0-9]{3,}` as a whole word. `dec-473`, `DEC 473`, `DEC-47` and `DEC-473_x` are read as no citation, so the commit is skipped without its tree being read.
- **Any Markdown file records an id.** A `.md` file anywhere in the commit's tree (a fixture, a template, a vendored doc) whose frontmatter has `id: DEC-473`, or any id with `type: decision`, counts as the record. The check does not look at where the file lies.
- **A register heading is enough.** `### DEC-500 — TBD` records DEC-500; neither the entry's body nor its status (rejected, superseded) is read. A heading inside a multi-line HTML comment also counts; only fenced code blocks are excluded.
- **Only `HEAD`'s history.** Commits on other branches and uncommitted work are not judged.
- **Severity.** The check definition is `severity: "warning"`, tier G1; whether a finding stops anything is decided by the runner, not here.

Two things do not fall through to clean: a named register that is absent, a link, a directory or not text gives `REGISTER_UNREADABLE` per citing commit, and every git or configuration failure exits 1 as `unmeasured`.
